none_means: No qualifying prior reference verified; not a proof of novelty.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a real-valued objective that may be nonconvex. The public starting point and gap bound satisfy f(x₀) − inf f ≤ Δ, with Δ ≥ 0. The infimum need not be attained.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.Instance, spec.valid and the inequality ∀ x, f q.x0 − f x ≤ q.Δ in spec.admissible.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Each call at x returns one vector g(x, ξ) with mean ∇f(x). Each call uses a fresh independent seed with the same law, including repeated calls at x. The parameters E, Ω, x₀, L₁, L₂, L₃, σ, Δ and ε are public. The objective, response map and sampling law are hidden. The oracle exposes only the returned vector.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.Query, spec.Reply and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean, IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: At every x, the centered squared error is integrable and E‖g(x, ξ) − ∇f(x)‖² ≤ σ². The public bound permits σ = 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and the centered second-moment conditions in spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The objective is C³. Its gradient, Hessian and third derivative are globally Lipschitz with respective public bounds L₁, L₂ and L₃, all strictly positive. The derivative bounds use induced operator norms. These smoothness conditions apply to f alone.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and the ContDiff and three Lipschitz conditions in spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The algorithm returns a measurable point X in E with integrable gradient norm. The criterion uses the first power of ‖∇f(X)‖.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: E‖∇f(X)‖ ≤ ε for the public tolerance ε > 0. The expectation covers both the algorithm seed and the oracle seeds. The oracle-call budget is a fixed cap on each run.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticThirdOrderSmoothNonconvex.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/Template.lean, OracleTemplate.Convergence and executeWithTrace.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation pairs a gradient-only, bounded-variance oracle with separate global controls on the Hessian and third derivative of the objective. Those higher-order bounds are available to the algorithm even though each query reveals only one noisy gradient.
